title: What If Halley's Comet Hit Earth Head-On?

scenes.text: What if Halley's Comet hit Earth? Its orbit makes it the worst possible visitor.
Its core is about 15 kilometers long and 8 wide, a flying mountain of ice and dust.
Every planet circles the Sun one way. Halley circles the other way, so it would meet us head-on.
In 1910 it passed Earth at about 70 kilometers per second, roughly 157,000 miles per hour.
Simple physics puts that hit near 100 million megatons of TNT, millions of times the biggest bomb ever tested.
Relax. Halley returns in 2061, and scientists see no closer pass for centuries. We are simply not in the way.

description:
What if Halley's Comet hit Earth head-on?
Its core is about 15 kilometers long and it moves against the planets' direction, so a hit would be at roughly 70 kilometers per second.
The good news: it is not coming our way. What should we run through next?
